title: Common definitions
description: Shared definitions so every schema uses one copy of each rule.

value_status.description: reported: the source gives a value. not_reported: the source gives none. not_applicable: no value applies (qualitative statement). excluded: the source reports a value, but FlameGuard-SI excludes it from use after a reviewed quality flag; the value is null here and stays as printed in the source file the locator points to.

value_matches_status.description: reported needs a non-null value; not_reported, not_applicable and excluded need null.

curation_note.description: A FlameGuard-SI quality assessment of a measured value. Never source text; source-reported uncertainty belongs in `uncertainty`. Every note carries a flag_ref and the source passage it rests on.

kind.description: Maps exactly to the quality-flag record's ranking_use as listed in x-flag-ranking-use (rule S10). A ranking_use of not_available produces no note: the finding is not_reported.

flag_ref.description: The reviewed quality-flag record behind this note (data/curated/interpretations/quality/). Required for every note. The schema checks only its shape: rule S10 requires it to resolve to a registered flag row whose ranking_use matches kind, and that row's NASA quote to be verified against the registered source text.

source.description: The NASA source passage the flag rests on, with its quote as recorded. The schema checks only that a non-empty quote is recorded. That does NOT authenticate it: a quote counts as verified only after rule S10(d) checks it against the registered source text (Member 3) and Member 5 checks it independently (Q3).

test_id.description: The source's own identifier for the test (as printed, e.g. a FLEX test number). A bare identifier, never prose. null means not reported.

test_outcome.description: Closed vocabulary from contracts/outcomes.json, as printed by the source for the test. null means not reported. While that list is empty (status UNCONFIRMED) only null is valid. Never free text.
